dualnicbc



Suite: dualnicbc (11 failures)


Suite TL;DR: A split-args bug in the newly introduced getClockIDViaPMC helper causes PMC commands to be rejected by the pmc binary, timing out all ClockSync tests; cascading config disruption and an event-consumer timeout account for the remaining failures.



Root Cause Groups:


• Group 1: PMC split-args bug in getClockIDViaPMC (affects: Slave can sync to master, Downstream slave can sync to BC master, Can provide a profile with higher priority)

• Evidence:

```

parentPortIdentity.clockIdentity not found in pmc output for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config: bad command: GET

bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET

grandmasterIdentity not found in pmc output for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config: bad command: GET

bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET

Timed out after 203.731s. / 203.074s. / 201.562s.

```


• Root Cause: getClockIDViaPMC in test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go (introduced in commit d20ffcbf0c, merged via 855c9e1493 2026-07-07) passes the pmc batch command as two separate slice elements — "GET" and "PARENT_DATA_SET" — rather than the single combined string "GET PARENT_DATA_SET":

```go

// BUGGY (ptphelper.go:144):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"}

// CORRECT (ptptesthelper.go:588, same repo):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET PARENT_DATA_SET"}

```

The linuxptp pmc binary processes each remaining argv element as a complete batch command. Receiving "GET" alone produces bad command: GET; "PARENT_DATA_SET" alone produces bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET. The getClockIDViaPMC fallback (reached when log-regex parsing misses the dualnicbc log format) therefore always fails, and the Eventually wrapper (3-minute timeout) exhausts before returning, failing these tests. bc-serial passes the equivalent tests because it finds the clock ID via log parsing and never reaches the broken pmc fallback.


• Breaking PR/Commit: d20ffcbf0c / merged 855c9e1493 — _"CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash"_ — test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go — [https://github.com/openshift/ptp-operator/commit/855c9e1493](https://github.com/openshift/ptp-operator/commit/855c9e1493)

• Is it a flake? No — the split-args bug produces bad command on every invocation, deterministically.

• Suggested Fix: Merge the two separate args into one in ptphelper.go: change "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET" to "GET PARENT_DATA_SET" as a single slice element, consistent with how GetClockClassViaPMC in ptptesthelper.go:588 already invokes pmc.


• Group 2: ptp4l clock class stuck at FREERUN (248) (affects: Verify clockClass when locking PTP source on dual NIC boundary clock, Should recover clockClass via event API after cloud-event-proxy crash, BC clock class recovers to Locked after upstream link outage)

• Evidence:

```

Timed out after 300.000s.

Expected PMC clock class 6 for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config

Expected : 248

to equal : 6

Timed out after 300.000s.

Expected ptp4l clock class to eventually be 6 for GM

Expected : false

to be true

```


• Root Cause: By the time these tests run (>670 s into the suite), test 3 ("Can provide a profile with higher priority") has timed out at 261 s while the temporary high-priority PtpConfig "temp" was still active. Although DeferCleanup(RestorePtp4lConf) fires, the ensuing ptp4l restart on the dualnicbc node means the second ptp4l instance (ptp4l.1) must re-acquire lock. The clockClass tests' 5-minute Eventually windows overlap with this re-sync period. Additionally, EnableGMCapableInPlace (used in test 4 at ptp.go:1256) explicitly injects clockClass 248 into the PtpConfig to create test conditions; if RestorePtp4lConf does not take effect fast enough before subsequent polling, all three clockClass assertions see 248. The correct GetClockClassViaPMC call format ("GET PARENT_DATA_SET" as a single arg at ptptesthelper.go:588) rules out the same pmc bug.

• Breaking PR/Commit: Same 855c9e1493 (test-ordering/cleanup-timing consequence of the Group 1 regression); no independent code regression confirmed for this group.

• Is it a flake? Partially — the cascade is deterministic given Group 1's timeouts, but the exact re-sync window makes this timing-sensitive.

• Suggested Fix: Fix Group 1 first; additionally add a post-DeferCleanup wait for ptp4l re-lock before handing off to the next test, and ensure EnableGMCapableInPlace is always accompanied by a synchronous restore check.


• Group 3: Interface role and process-state cascade (affects: The slave node network interface is taken down and up, Should restart phc2sys with no socket errors after SIGTERM, PTP metric is present verifies on slave)

• Evidence:

```

Timed out after 300.001s.

ens2f0np0 should recover to SLAVE

incorrect role for ens2f0np0, role expected=1(SLAVE), role observed=2(MASTER)


Timed out after 180.001s.

Expected phc2sys process status to be 1 for GM

Expected : 0

to equal : 1


Timed out after 300.000s.

Time metrics are not detected

```


• Root Cause: With ptp4l.1 in FREERUN (clock class 248, no upstream lock — see Group 2), the port that should be SLAVE (ens2f0np0) remains in MASTER role because ptp4l acts as a grandmaster candidate. phc2sys does not start when ptp4l is unlocked (process status=0). PTP time-sync metrics (openshift_ptp_*) are not emitted without a locked clock state. All three symptoms are downstream of the same unlocked ptp4l.1 state, compounded by the config disruption from Group 1/2.

• Breaking PR/Commit: Same cascade from 855c9e1493. No independent breaking commit identified.

• Is it a flake? No — deterministic cascade.

• Suggested Fix: Resolving Group 1 and ensuring clean state restore between tests (Group 2) should clear these failures.


• Group 4: Event consumer pod log deadline (affects: Should receive events after linuxptp-daemon pod restart, [dualnicbc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync)

• Evidence:

```

getCurrentState did not return SyncStateChange

error reading logs in ns=ptp-event-framework-test pod=consumer: context deadline exceeded


could not push initial event, err=error reading logs in ns=ptp-event-framework-test pod=consumer: context deadline exceeded

```


• Root Cause: Both the serial and parallel event tests fail because the consumer pod in namespace ptp-event-framework-test does not emit logs within the deadline. This consumer pod is established by the event test setup and depends on the cloud-event-proxy sidecar publishing a SyncStateChange event; with ptp4l in FREERUN (Group 2), no valid sync-state transition is ever published, so the consumer pod log stream never produces the expected line and the context deadline fires. The parallel test independently hits the same consumer pod and likewise times out.

• Breaking PR/Commit: Cascade from Group 2; event framework code unchanged. Unknown if there is a separate event-consumer pod startup bug.

The test ran for ~363 seconds without ever receiving a LOCKED event. The simultaneous failure of the same event-based test across all 5 parallel suites (bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc), plus serial PTP-sync failures in dualnicbc/dualnicbcha/tgm/tbc suites in the same run, points to the PTP grandmaster-to-slave synchronization chain being degraded or disconnected on the RDU2 test hardware during this job window rather than any code regression.
• Breaking PR/Commit: Unknown — no code change identified; this is a hardware/infrastructure timing failure. Test code on main already includes commit 4aa5310 (ci: fix timeout onPushInitialEvent) which extended PushInitialEvent retries to 30×10s for exactly this class of slow-start scenario. The release-5.0 images are built from release-5.0 branch. No new cherry-pick or release-5.0 code change identified as a trigger.
• Is it a flake? yes — simultaneous failure across 5 independent parallel suites on the same hardware node pool at the same wall-clock time is the hallmark of a transient infra condition (PTP GM link loss, NIC reset, or environmental timing glitch), not a reproducible code defect. The dualfollower serial suite's configuration-verification tests all passed in the same run.
• Suggested Fix: Re-run the job to confirm this is transient. If it recurs, check whether the PTP grandmaster at cnfdf30/cnfdf31/cnfdf32 (RDU2 telco5g lab) was in holdover or FREERUN during the test window by examining the must-gather artifacts and pod-logs collected at post-step; longer-term, the test could be made more resilient by retrying the entire soak test when zero LOCKED events are observed within the first few minutes.

Suite Issue Class: test_flake

Suite Severity: MEDIUM


dualnicbc



Suite: dualnicbc (11 failures)


Suite TL;DR: A split-args bug in the newly introduced getClockIDViaPMC helper causes PMC commands to be rejected by the pmc binary, timing out all ClockSync tests; cascading config disruption and an event-consumer timeout account for the remaining failures.



Root Cause Groups:


• Group 1: PMC split-args bug in getClockIDViaPMC (affects: Slave can sync to master, Downstream slave can sync to BC master, Can provide a profile with higher priority)

• Evidence:

```

parentPortIdentity.clockIdentity not found in pmc output for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config: bad command: GET

bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET

grandmasterIdentity not found in pmc output for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config: bad command: GET

bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET

Timed out after 203.731s. / 203.074s. / 201.562s.

```


• Root Cause: getClockIDViaPMC in test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go (introduced in commit d20ffcbf0c, merged via 855c9e1493 2026-07-07) passes the pmc batch command as two separate slice elements — "GET" and "PARENT_DATA_SET" — rather than the single combined string "GET PARENT_DATA_SET":

```go

// BUGGY (ptphelper.go:144):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"}

// CORRECT (ptptesthelper.go:588, same repo):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET PARENT_DATA_SET"}

```

The linuxptp pmc binary processes each remaining argv element as a complete batch command. Receiving "GET" alone produces bad command: GET; "PARENT_DATA_SET" alone produces bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET. The getClockIDViaPMC fallback (reached when log-regex parsing misses the dualnicbc log format) therefore always fails, and the Eventually wrapper (3-minute timeout) exhausts before returning, failing these tests. bc-serial passes the equivalent tests because it finds the clock ID via log parsing and never reaches the broken pmc fallback.


• Breaking PR/Commit: d20ffcbf0c / merged 855c9e1493 — _"CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash"_ — test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go — [https://github.com/openshift/ptp-operator/commit/855c9e1493](https://github.com/openshift/ptp-operator/commit/855c9e1493)

• Is it a flake? No — the split-args bug produces bad command on every invocation, deterministically.

• Suggested Fix: Merge the two separate args into one in ptphelper.go: change "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET" to "GET PARENT_DATA_SET" as a single slice element, consistent with how GetClockClassViaPMC in ptptesthelper.go:588 already invokes pmc.


• Group 2: ptp4l clock class stuck at FREERUN (248) (affects: Verify clockClass when locking PTP source on dual NIC boundary clock, Should recover clockClass via event API after cloud-event-proxy crash, BC clock class recovers to Locked after upstream link outage)

• Evidence:

```

Timed out after 300.000s.

Expected PMC clock class 6 for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config

Expected : 248

to equal : 6

Timed out after 300.000s.

Expected ptp4l clock class to eventually be 6 for GM

Expected : false

to be true

```


• Root Cause: By the time these tests run (>670 s into the suite), test 3 ("Can provide a profile with higher priority") has timed out at 261 s while the temporary high-priority PtpConfig "temp" was still active. Although DeferCleanup(RestorePtp4lConf) fires, the ensuing ptp4l restart on the dualnicbc node means the second ptp4l instance (ptp4l.1) must re-acquire lock. The clockClass tests' 5-minute Eventually windows overlap with this re-sync period. Additionally, EnableGMCapableInPlace (used in test 4 at ptp.go:1256) explicitly injects clockClass 248 into the PtpConfig to create test conditions; if RestorePtp4lConf does not take effect fast enough before subsequent polling, all three clockClass assertions see 248. The correct GetClockClassViaPMC call format ("GET PARENT_DATA_SET" as a single arg at ptptesthelper.go:588) rules out the same pmc bug.

• Breaking PR/Commit: Same 855c9e1493 (test-ordering/cleanup-timing consequence of the Group 1 regression); no independent code regression confirmed for this group.

• Is it a flake? Partially — the cascade is deterministic given Group 1's timeouts, but the exact re-sync window makes this timing-sensitive.

• Suggested Fix: Fix Group 1 first; additionally add a post-DeferCleanup wait for ptp4l re-lock before handing off to the next test, and ensure EnableGMCapableInPlace is always accompanied by a synchronous restore check.


• Group 3: Interface role and process-state cascade (affects: The slave node network interface is taken down and up, Should restart phc2sys with no socket errors after SIGTERM, PTP metric is present verifies on slave)

• Evidence:

```

Timed out after 300.001s.

ens2f0np0 should recover to SLAVE

incorrect role for ens2f0np0, role expected=1(SLAVE), role observed=2(MASTER)


Timed out after 180.001s.

Expected phc2sys process status to be 1 for GM

Expected : 0

to equal : 1


Timed out after 300.000s.

Time metrics are not detected

```


• Root Cause: With ptp4l.1 in FREERUN (clock class 248, no upstream lock — see Group 2), the port that should be SLAVE (ens2f0np0) remains in MASTER role because ptp4l acts as a grandmaster candidate. phc2sys does not start when ptp4l is unlocked (process status=0). PTP time-sync metrics (openshift_ptp_*) are not emitted without a locked clock state. All three symptoms are downstream of the same unlocked ptp4l.1 state, compounded by the config disruption from Group 1/2.

• Breaking PR/Commit: Same cascade from 855c9e1493. No independent breaking commit identified.

• Is it a flake? No — deterministic cascade.

• Suggested Fix: Resolving Group 1 and ensuring clean state restore between tests (Group 2) should clear these failures.


• Group 4: Event consumer pod log deadline (affects: Should receive events after linuxptp-daemon pod restart, [dualnicbc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync)

• Evidence:

```

getCurrentState did not return SyncStateChange

error reading logs in ns=ptp-event-framework-test pod=consumer: context deadline exceeded


could not push initial event, err=error reading logs in ns=ptp-event-framework-test pod=consumer: context deadline exceeded

```


• Root Cause: Both the serial and parallel event tests fail because the consumer pod in namespace ptp-event-framework-test does not emit logs within the deadline. This consumer pod is established by the event test setup and depends on the cloud-event-proxy sidecar publishing a SyncStateChange event; with ptp4l in FREERUN (Group 2), no valid sync-state transition is ever published, so the consumer pod log stream never produces the expected line and the context deadline fires. The parallel test independently hits the same consumer pod and likewise times out.

• Breaking PR/Commit: Cascade from Group 2; event framework code unchanged. Unknown if there is a separate event-consumer pod startup bug.

Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp


TL;DR: Hardware sync failures across RDU2 nodes and a deterministic PMC split-args code bug together account for 36 test failures spanning all 7 suites.



Root Cause Groups


#DescriptionCountSuites
1T-GM ts2phc stuck in FREERUN on cnfdf32 — DPLL shows LOCKED but ts2phc reports FREERUN; daemon gate blocks phc2sys, clockClass never reaches 6, cascading to event/metric/holdover failures11 / 36tgm
2BC slave port ens2f0np0 / hardware clock sync degradation — BC slave stuck in MASTER state; ptp4l clockClass stuck at 248 (FREERUN) on dualnicbc nodes; cascading to config, event-consumer, and interface-recovery tests~14 / 36dualnicbc (5–6), dualnicbcha (8–9)
3PMC split-args bug in getClockIDViaPMC — commits 3b93c9f408 / d20ffcbf0c pass "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET" as two separate argv elements; pmc rejects both with bad command; all ClockSync tests time out deterministically~5 / 36dualnicbc (3), dualnicbcha (2)
4Parallel event soak test timeout (OCPBUGS-60570 interaction) — PushInitialEvent retry loop (up to 30 × 10 s = 300 s) shares the same 6-minute soak timer; release-5.0 image fix (OCPBUGS-60570) slows initial event delivery, exhausting the budget before LOCKED is received; all 5 parallel suites hit this simultaneously pointing to a cluster-wide event delivery slowdown5 / 36bc (1), dualfollower (1), oc (1), dualnicbc (1), dualnicbcha (1)
5No T-BC topology on cluster — CreatePtpConfigurationsWithRetry finds 0 T-BC L2 solutions on cnfdf30–32; execute.BeforeAll calls Fail() instead of Skip(), failing the first spec and silently skipping the rest1 / 36tbc


Cross-Suite Patterns


• Hardware sync failure is the dominant cross-suite thread. Root causes 1 and 2 both point to the RDU2 test nodes (cnfdf30–32) failing to maintain a healthy PTP grandmaster-to-slave chain during this job window. tgm (ts2phc FREERUN on the GM node) and dualnicbc/dualnicbcha (clockClass/port-state failures on BC nodes) are facets of the same degraded physical sync fabric.

• The PMC split-args bug (root cause 3) is strictly test-code and suite-independent. It affects every suite that exercises the getClockIDViaPMC fallback path — currently triggered only in dualnicbc and dualnicbcha because their log format misses the primary log-parsing path. bc-serial escapes because it locates the clock ID via log parsing before reaching the broken fallback.

• The parallel soak timeout (root cause 4) is cross-suite by construction. All five parallel sub-suites (bc-parallel, dualfollower-parallel, dualnicbc-parallel, dualnicbcha-parallel, oc-parallel) run the same testSyncState test against the same cluster-event infrastructure. Their simultaneous failure at ≈363 seconds is a single shared event, not five independent regressions.

• Suite-specific failures: tbc's BeforeAll topology failure is isolated to that suite; tgm's ts2phc FREERUN affects only the GM node tests.


Actionable Recommendations


1. Fix the PMC split-args bug immediately (highest leverage, deterministic, trivially patched).

In test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go (around line 144), change:

```go

// current (broken):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"}

// fix:

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET PARENT_DATA_SET"}

```

This matches the existing pattern in ptptesthelper.go:588 (GetClockClassViaPMC) and will immediately unblock ~5 deterministically failing tests in dualnicbc and dualnicbcha.


2. Investigate and remediate the RDU2 hardware sync chain (cnfdf30–32).

Both the ts2phc FREERUN (tgm) and the BC slave MASTER-state / clockClass-248 failures (dualnicbc, dualnicbcha) trace to the physical PTP grandmaster-to-slave path being degraded during this run window. Check GNSS/GPS signal quality on the GM node, verify the T-GM NIC (ens7fx/WPC card) cable and SFP state, and confirm DPLL lock propagation from GM to BC nodes before re-running.


3. Decouple PushInitialEvent retries from the soak timer, and add a Skip path for missing topologies.

For root cause 4: run the PushInitialEvent retry loop before starting tcEndChan, or extend the parallel soak window to accommodate the OCPBUGS-60570 slow-start behavior.

For root cause 5 (tbc): replace the Fail("Could not create a ptp config…") call in execute.BeforeAll with a Skip(...) when no topology is found, preventing misleading failures when the cluster lacks T-BC hardware.



Overall Issue Class


infra_other + test_regression (mixed: ~21 failures are hardware/infra-driven; ~5 are a deterministic test code bug; 5 are a test/infra interaction flake; 1 is a topology mismatch)


Overall Severity


HIGH — 36 failures spanning all 7 suites; two root causes are entirely blocking for their affected suites (ts2phc FREERUN, BC slave MASTER state), and one is a trivially fixable deterministic code regression that has been silently breaking ClockSync tests across at least two suites.




Per-Suite Details



bc



Suite: bc (1 failures)


Suite TL;DR: The single bc failure is the event-based PTP Slave Clock Sync test timing out because the OS clock never reached LOCKED state (as reported via PTP events) within the test's monitoring window.


Root Cause Groups:


• Group 1: OS clock never reported LOCKED via PTP events within test duration (affects: [It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync)
• Evidence:
• From investigation-summary.txt: Source: parallel_suite_test.go:117, parallel_suite_test.go:90, ptp.go:393, run.go:84
• From telco5g-ptp-tests__test_results.json: "[It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync": {"time": 363.837272163, "result": "error"}
• From ptp.go (line 392–393): if !wasLocked { Fail("OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out") }
• From ptp.go (lines 355, 371–373): const maxPushInitialEventAttempts = 30 … for i = 0; i < maxPushInitialEventAttempts; i++ { err = event.PushInitialEvent(string(ptpEvent.OsClockSyncStateChange), 10*time.Second)
• From ci-operator-build-log.txt (line 40–42): + export PTP_UNDER_TEST_BRANCH=release-5.0 … + export IMG_VERSION=release-5.0
• From ci-operator-build-log.txt (line 37): + export TEST_BRANCH=main — test scripts run from main against release-5.0 production images
• Root Cause: In test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go, the testSyncState function subscribes to OsClockSyncStateChange events and waits up to the configured soak-test duration for the OS clock to report LOCKED. The test ran for 363 seconds (≈ ~60 s of PushInitialEvent retries + a ~5-minute soak window), matching the tcEndChan path at ptp.go:393. Commit 4aa5310 on main ("ci: fix timeout onPushInitialEvent") introduced the 30-retry loop specifically because OCPBUGS-60570 changed release-5.0 cloud-event-proxy to only serve CurrentState from real PTP socket data. Despite eventually getting an initial event, the OsClockSyncStateChange events never carried a LOCKED state before the soak period expired — indicating the OS clock did not lock during that window on the test cluster. This same pattern recurs in all five parallel suites (bc-parallel, dualfollower-parallel, dualnicbc-parallel, dualnicbcha-parallel, oc-parallel), pointing to a systemic sync or event-delivery problem rather than a BC-specific regression.
• Breaking PR/Commit: Upstream behavioral change tracked in OCPBUGS-60570 (backported to release-5.0 cloud-event-proxy images); test-side adaptation landed in main commit 4aa5310 ("ci: fix timeout onPushInitialEvent"). No single cherry-pick SHA identified as the trigger; the OCPBUGS-60570 image change is the underlying cause.
• Is it a flake? Possibly — the identical test failing simultaneously across all five parallel suites in the same run (bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc) suggests a systemic cluster-level sync failure for this specific run rather than a permanent regression. The test has a documented history of timing sensitivity (hence commit 4aa5310). A single retry of the periodic job is warranted before escalating.
• Suggested Fix: Verify whether the BC node's OS clock is actually achieving LOCKED state during test runs by inspecting phc2sys logs; if the clock is locking but events aren't delivered, investigate whether the release-5.0 cloud-event-proxy OsClockSyncStateChange publication path is broken. If this is reproducible, raise a bug against the release-5.0 cloud-event-proxy image referencing OCPBUGS-60570 and confirm the fix is correctly backported.

3PMC split-args bug in getClockIDViaPMC — commits 3b93c9f408 / d20ffcbf0c pass "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET" as two separate argv elements; pmc rejects both with bad command; all ClockSync tests time out deterministically~5 / 36dualnicbc (3), dualnicbcha (2)

Cross-Suite Patterns


• Hardware sync failure is the dominant cross-suite thread. Root causes 1 and 2 both point to the RDU2 test nodes (cnfdf30–32) failing to maintain a healthy PTP grandmaster-to-slave chain during this job window. tgm (ts2phc FREERUN on the GM node) and dualnicbc/dualnicbcha (clockClass/port-state failures on BC nodes) are facets of the same degraded physical sync fabric.

• The PMC split-args bug (root cause 3) is strictly test-code and suite-independent. It affects every suite that exercises the getClockIDViaPMC fallback path — currently triggered only in dualnicbc and dualnicbcha because their log format misses the primary log-parsing path. bc-serial escapes because it locates the clock ID via log parsing before reaching the broken fallback.

• The parallel soak timeout (root cause 4) is cross-suite by construction. All five parallel sub-suites (bc-parallel, dualfollower-parallel, dualnicbc-parallel, dualnicbcha-parallel, oc-parallel) run the same testSyncState test against the same cluster-event infrastructure. Their simultaneous failure at ≈363 seconds is a single shared event, not five independent regressions.

• Suite-specific failures: tbc's BeforeAll topology failure is isolated to that suite; tgm's ts2phc FREERUN affects only the GM node tests.


Actionable Recommendations


1. Fix the PMC split-args bug immediately (highest leverage, deterministic, trivially patched).

In test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go (around line 144), change:

```go

// current (broken):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"}

// fix:

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET PARENT_DATA_SET"}

```

This matches the existing pattern in ptptesthelper.go:588 (GetClockClassViaPMC) and will immediately unblock ~5 deterministically failing tests in dualnicbc and dualnicbcha.


2. Investigate and remediate the RDU2 hardware sync chain (cnfdf30–32).

Both the ts2phc FREERUN (tgm) and the BC slave MASTER-state / clockClass-248 failures (dualnicbc, dualnicbcha) trace to the physical PTP grandmaster-to-slave path being degraded during this run window. Check GNSS/GPS signal quality on the GM node, verify the T-GM NIC (ens7fx/WPC card) cable and SFP state, and confirm DPLL lock propagation from GM to BC nodes before re-running.


3. Decouple PushInitialEvent retries from the soak timer, and add a Skip path for missing topologies.

For root cause 4: run the PushInitialEvent retry loop before starting tcEndChan, or extend the parallel soak window to accommodate the OCPBUGS-60570 slow-start behavior.

For root cause 5 (tbc): replace the Fail("Could not create a ptp config…") call in execute.BeforeAll with a Skip(...) when no topology is found, preventing misleading failures when the cluster lacks T-BC hardware.

infra_other + test_regression (mixed: ~21 failures are hardware/infra-driven; ~5 are a deterministic test code bug; 5 are a test/infra interaction flake; 1 is a topology mismatch)


Overall Severity


HIGH — 36 failures spanning all 7 suites; two root causes are entirely blocking for their affected suites (ts2phc FREERUN, BC slave MASTER state), and one is a trivially fixable deterministic code regression that has been silently breaking ClockSync tests across at least two suites.

Suite: bc (1 failures)


Suite TL;DR: The single bc failure is the event-based PTP Slave Clock Sync test timing out because the OS clock never reached LOCKED state (as reported via PTP events) within the test's monitoring window.


Root Cause Groups:


• Group 1: OS clock never reported LOCKED via PTP events within test duration (affects: [It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync)
• Evidence:
• From investigation-summary.txt: Source: parallel_suite_test.go:117, parallel_suite_test.go:90, ptp.go:393, run.go:84
• From telco5g-ptp-tests__test_results.json: "[It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync": {"time": 363.837272163, "result": "error"}
• From ptp.go (line 392–393): if !wasLocked { Fail("OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out") }
• From ptp.go (lines 355, 371–373): const maxPushInitialEventAttempts = 30 … for i = 0; i < maxPushInitialEventAttempts; i++ { err = event.PushInitialEvent(string(ptpEvent.OsClockSyncStateChange), 10*time.Second)
• From ci-operator-build-log.txt (line 40–42): + export PTP_UNDER_TEST_BRANCH=release-5.0 … + export IMG_VERSION=release-5.0
• From ci-operator-build-log.txt (line 37): + export TEST_BRANCH=main — test scripts run from main against release-5.0 production images
• Root Cause: In test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go, the testSyncState function subscribes to OsClockSyncStateChange events and waits up to the configured soak-test duration for the OS clock to report LOCKED. The test ran for 363 seconds (≈ ~60 s of PushInitialEvent retries + a ~5-minute soak window), matching the tcEndChan path at ptp.go:393. Commit 4aa5310 on main ("ci: fix timeout onPushInitialEvent") introduced the 30-retry loop specifically because OCPBUGS-60570 changed release-5.0 cloud-event-proxy to only serve CurrentState from real PTP socket data. Despite eventually getting an initial event, the OsClockSyncStateChange events never carried a LOCKED state before the soak period expired — indicating the OS clock did not lock during that window on the test cluster. This same pattern recurs in all five parallel suites (bc-parallel, dualfollower-parallel, dualnicbc-parallel, dualnicbcha-parallel, oc-parallel), pointing to a systemic sync or event-delivery problem rather than a BC-specific regression.
• Breaking PR/Commit: Upstream behavioral change tracked in OCPBUGS-60570 (backported to release-5.0 cloud-event-proxy images); test-side adaptation landed in main commit 4aa5310 ("ci: fix timeout onPushInitialEvent"). No single cherry-pick SHA identified as the trigger; the OCPBUGS-60570 image change is the underlying cause.
• Is it a flake? Possibly — the identical test failing simultaneously across all five parallel suites in the same run (bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc) suggests a systemic cluster-level sync failure for this specific run rather than a permanent regression. The test has a documented history of timing sensitivity (hence commit 4aa5310). A single retry of the periodic job is warranted before escalating.
• Suggested Fix: Verify whether the BC node's OS clock is actually achieving LOCKED state during test runs by inspecting phc2sys logs; if the clock is locking but events aren't delivered, investigate whether the release-5.0 cloud-event-proxy OsClockSyncStateChange publication path is broken. If this is reproducible, raise a bug against the release-5.0 cloud-event-proxy image referencing OCPBUGS-60570 and confirm the fix is correctly backported.

dualnicbc



Suite: dualnicbc (11 failures)


Suite TL;DR: A split-args bug in the newly introduced getClockIDViaPMC helper causes PMC commands to be rejected by the pmc binary, timing out all ClockSync tests; cascading config disruption and an event-consumer timeout account for the remaining failures.



Root Cause Groups:


• Group 1: PMC split-args bug in getClockIDViaPMC (affects: Slave can sync to master, Downstream slave can sync to BC master, Can provide a profile with higher priority)

• Evidence:

```

parentPortIdentity.clockIdentity not found in pmc output for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config: bad command: GET

bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET

grandmasterIdentity not found in pmc output for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config: bad command: GET

bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET

Timed out after 203.731s. / 203.074s. / 201.562s.

```


• Root Cause: getClockIDViaPMC in test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go (introduced in commit d20ffcbf0c, merged via 855c9e1493 2026-07-07) passes the pmc batch command as two separate slice elements — "GET" and "PARENT_DATA_SET" — rather than the single combined string "GET PARENT_DATA_SET":

```go

// BUGGY (ptphelper.go:144):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"}

// CORRECT (ptptesthelper.go:588, same repo):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET PARENT_DATA_SET"}

```

The linuxptp pmc binary processes each remaining argv element as a complete batch command. Receiving "GET" alone produces bad command: GET; "PARENT_DATA_SET" alone produces bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET. The getClockIDViaPMC fallback (reached when log-regex parsing misses the dualnicbc log format) therefore always fails, and the Eventually wrapper (3-minute timeout) exhausts before returning, failing these tests. bc-serial passes the equivalent tests because it finds the clock ID via log parsing and never reaches the broken pmc fallback.


• Breaking PR/Commit: d20ffcbf0c / merged 855c9e1493 — _"CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash"_ — test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go — [https://github.com/openshift/ptp-operator/commit/855c9e1493](https://github.com/openshift/ptp-operator/commit/855c9e1493)

• Is it a flake? No — the split-args bug produces bad command on every invocation, deterministically.

• Suggested Fix: Merge the two separate args into one in ptphelper.go: change "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET" to "GET PARENT_DATA_SET" as a single slice element, consistent with how GetClockClassViaPMC in ptptesthelper.go:588 already invokes pmc.


• Group 2: ptp4l clock class stuck at FREERUN (248) (affects: Verify clockClass when locking PTP source on dual NIC boundary clock, Should recover clockClass via event API after cloud-event-proxy crash, BC clock class recovers to Locked after upstream link outage)

• Evidence:

```

Timed out after 300.000s.

Expected PMC clock class 6 for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config

Expected : 248

to equal : 6

Timed out after 300.000s.

Expected ptp4l clock class to eventually be 6 for GM

Expected : false

to be true

```


• Root Cause: By the time these tests run (>670 s into the suite), test 3 ("Can provide a profile with higher priority") has timed out at 261 s while the temporary high-priority PtpConfig "temp" was still active. Although DeferCleanup(RestorePtp4lConf) fires, the ensuing ptp4l restart on the dualnicbc node means the second ptp4l instance (ptp4l.1) must re-acquire lock. The clockClass tests' 5-minute Eventually windows overlap with this re-sync period. Additionally, EnableGMCapableInPlace (used in test 4 at ptp.go:1256) explicitly injects clockClass 248 into the PtpConfig to create test conditions; if RestorePtp4lConf does not take effect fast enough before subsequent polling, all three clockClass assertions see 248. The correct GetClockClassViaPMC call format ("GET PARENT_DATA_SET" as a single arg at ptptesthelper.go:588) rules out the same pmc bug.

• Breaking PR/Commit: Same 855c9e1493 (test-ordering/cleanup-timing consequence of the Group 1 regression); no independent code regression confirmed for this group.

• Is it a flake? Partially — the cascade is deterministic given Group 1's timeouts, but the exact re-sync window makes this timing-sensitive.

• Suggested Fix: Fix Group 1 first; additionally add a post-DeferCleanup wait for ptp4l re-lock before handing off to the next test, and ensure EnableGMCapableInPlace is always accompanied by a synchronous restore check.


• Group 3: Interface role and process-state cascade (affects: The slave node network interface is taken down and up, Should restart phc2sys with no socket errors after SIGTERM, PTP metric is present verifies on slave)

• Evidence:

```

Timed out after 300.001s.

ens2f0np0 should recover to SLAVE

incorrect role for ens2f0np0, role expected=1(SLAVE), role observed=2(MASTER)


Timed out after 180.001s.

Expected phc2sys process status to be 1 for GM

Expected : 0

to equal : 1


Timed out after 300.000s.

Time metrics are not detected

```


• Root Cause: With ptp4l.1 in FREERUN (clock class 248, no upstream lock — see Group 2), the port that should be SLAVE (ens2f0np0) remains in MASTER role because ptp4l acts as a grandmaster candidate. phc2sys does not start when ptp4l is unlocked (process status=0). PTP time-sync metrics (openshift_ptp_*) are not emitted without a locked clock state. All three symptoms are downstream of the same unlocked ptp4l.1 state, compounded by the config disruption from Group 1/2.

• Breaking PR/Commit: Same cascade from 855c9e1493. No independent breaking commit identified.

• Is it a flake? No — deterministic cascade.

• Suggested Fix: Resolving Group 1 and ensuring clean state restore between tests (Group 2) should clear these failures.


• Group 4: Event consumer pod log deadline (affects: Should receive events after linuxptp-daemon pod restart, [dualnicbc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync)

• Evidence:

```

getCurrentState did not return SyncStateChange

error reading logs in ns=ptp-event-framework-test pod=consumer: context deadline exceeded


could not push initial event, err=error reading logs in ns=ptp-event-framework-test pod=consumer: context deadline exceeded

```


• Root Cause: Both the serial and parallel event tests fail because the consumer pod in namespace ptp-event-framework-test does not emit logs within the deadline. This consumer pod is established by the event test setup and depends on the cloud-event-proxy sidecar publishing a SyncStateChange event; with ptp4l in FREERUN (Group 2), no valid sync-state transition is ever published, so the consumer pod log stream never produces the expected line and the context deadline fires. The parallel test independently hits the same consumer pod and likewise times out.

• Breaking PR/Commit: Cascade from Group 2; event framework code unchanged. Unknown if there is a separate event-consumer pod startup bug.

The test ran for ~363 seconds without ever receiving a LOCKED event. The simultaneous failure of the same event-based test across all 5 parallel suites (bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc), plus serial PTP-sync failures in dualnicbc/dualnicbcha/tgm/tbc suites in the same run, points to the PTP grandmaster-to-slave synchronization chain being degraded or disconnected on the RDU2 test hardware during this job window rather than any code regression.
• Breaking PR/Commit: Unknown — no code change identified; this is a hardware/infrastructure timing failure. Test code on main already includes commit 4aa5310 (ci: fix timeout onPushInitialEvent) which extended PushInitialEvent retries to 30×10s for exactly this class of slow-start scenario. The release-5.0 images are built from release-5.0 branch. No new cherry-pick or release-5.0 code change identified as a trigger.
• Is it a flake? yes — simultaneous failure across 5 independent parallel suites on the same hardware node pool at the same wall-clock time is the hallmark of a transient infra condition (PTP GM link loss, NIC reset, or environmental timing glitch), not a reproducible code defect. The dualfollower serial suite's configuration-verification tests all passed in the same run.
• Suggested Fix: Re-run the job to confirm this is transient. If it recurs, check whether the PTP grandmaster at cnfdf30/cnfdf31/cnfdf32 (RDU2 telco5g lab) was in holdover or FREERUN during the test window by examining the must-gather artifacts and pod-logs collected at post-step; longer-term, the test could be made more resilient by retrying the entire soak test when zero LOCKED events are observed within the first few minutes.

Suite Issue Class: test_flake

Suite Severity: MEDIUM


dualnicbc



Suite: dualnicbc (11 failures)


Suite TL;DR: A split-args bug in the newly introduced getClockIDViaPMC helper causes PMC commands to be rejected by the pmc binary, timing out all ClockSync tests; cascading config disruption and an event-consumer timeout account for the remaining failures.



Root Cause Groups:


• Group 1: PMC split-args bug in getClockIDViaPMC (affects: Slave can sync to master, Downstream slave can sync to BC master, Can provide a profile with higher priority)

• Evidence:

```

parentPortIdentity.clockIdentity not found in pmc output for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config: bad command: GET

bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET

grandmasterIdentity not found in pmc output for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config: bad command: GET

bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET

Timed out after 203.731s. / 203.074s. / 201.562s.

```


• Root Cause: getClockIDViaPMC in test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go (introduced in commit d20ffcbf0c, merged via 855c9e1493 2026-07-07) passes the pmc batch command as two separate slice elements — "GET" and "PARENT_DATA_SET" — rather than the single combined string "GET PARENT_DATA_SET":

```go

// BUGGY (ptphelper.go:144):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"}

// CORRECT (ptptesthelper.go:588, same repo):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET PARENT_DATA_SET"}

```

The linuxptp pmc binary processes each remaining argv element as a complete batch command. Receiving "GET" alone produces bad command: GET; "PARENT_DATA_SET" alone produces bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET. The getClockIDViaPMC fallback (reached when log-regex parsing misses the dualnicbc log format) therefore always fails, and the Eventually wrapper (3-minute timeout) exhausts before returning, failing these tests. bc-serial passes the equivalent tests because it finds the clock ID via log parsing and never reaches the broken pmc fallback.


• Breaking PR/Commit: d20ffcbf0c / merged 855c9e1493 — _"CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash"_ — test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go — [https://github.com/openshift/ptp-operator/commit/855c9e1493](https://github.com/openshift/ptp-operator/commit/855c9e1493)

• Is it a flake? No — the split-args bug produces bad command on every invocation, deterministically.

• Suggested Fix: Merge the two separate args into one in ptphelper.go: change "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET" to "GET PARENT_DATA_SET" as a single slice element, consistent with how GetClockClassViaPMC in ptptesthelper.go:588 already invokes pmc.


• Group 2: ptp4l clock class stuck at FREERUN (248) (affects: Verify clockClass when locking PTP source on dual NIC boundary clock, Should recover clockClass via event API after cloud-event-proxy crash, BC clock class recovers to Locked after upstream link outage)

• Evidence:

```

Timed out after 300.000s.

Expected PMC clock class 6 for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config

Expected : 248

to equal : 6

Timed out after 300.000s.

Expected ptp4l clock class to eventually be 6 for GM

Expected : false

to be true

```


• Root Cause: By the time these tests run (>670 s into the suite), test 3 ("Can provide a profile with higher priority") has timed out at 261 s while the temporary high-priority PtpConfig "temp" was still active. Although DeferCleanup(RestorePtp4lConf) fires, the ensuing ptp4l restart on the dualnicbc node means the second ptp4l instance (ptp4l.1) must re-acquire lock. The clockClass tests' 5-minute Eventually windows overlap with this re-sync period. Additionally, EnableGMCapableInPlace (used in test 4 at ptp.go:1256) explicitly injects clockClass 248 into the PtpConfig to create test conditions; if RestorePtp4lConf does not take effect fast enough before subsequent polling, all three clockClass assertions see 248. The correct GetClockClassViaPMC call format ("GET PARENT_DATA_SET" as a single arg at ptptesthelper.go:588) rules out the same pmc bug.

• Breaking PR/Commit: Same 855c9e1493 (test-ordering/cleanup-timing consequence of the Group 1 regression); no independent code regression confirmed for this group.

• Is it a flake? Partially — the cascade is deterministic given Group 1's timeouts, but the exact re-sync window makes this timing-sensitive.

• Suggested Fix: Fix Group 1 first; additionally add a post-DeferCleanup wait for ptp4l re-lock before handing off to the next test, and ensure EnableGMCapableInPlace is always accompanied by a synchronous restore check.


• Group 3: Interface role and process-state cascade (affects: The slave node network interface is taken down and up, Should restart phc2sys with no socket errors after SIGTERM, PTP metric is present verifies on slave)

• Evidence:

```

Timed out after 300.001s.

ens2f0np0 should recover to SLAVE

incorrect role for ens2f0np0, role expected=1(SLAVE), role observed=2(MASTER)


Timed out after 180.001s.

Expected phc2sys process status to be 1 for GM

Expected : 0

to equal : 1


Timed out after 300.000s.

Time metrics are not detected

```


• Root Cause: With ptp4l.1 in FREERUN (clock class 248, no upstream lock — see Group 2), the port that should be SLAVE (ens2f0np0) remains in MASTER role because ptp4l acts as a grandmaster candidate. phc2sys does not start when ptp4l is unlocked (process status=0). PTP time-sync metrics (openshift_ptp_*) are not emitted without a locked clock state. All three symptoms are downstream of the same unlocked ptp4l.1 state, compounded by the config disruption from Group 1/2.

• Breaking PR/Commit: Same cascade from 855c9e1493. No independent breaking commit identified.

• Is it a flake? No — deterministic cascade.

• Suggested Fix: Resolving Group 1 and ensuring clean state restore between tests (Group 2) should clear these failures.


• Group 4: Event consumer pod log deadline (affects: Should receive events after linuxptp-daemon pod restart, [dualnicbc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync)

• Evidence:

```

getCurrentState did not return SyncStateChange

error reading logs in ns=ptp-event-framework-test pod=consumer: context deadline exceeded


could not push initial event, err=error reading logs in ns=ptp-event-framework-test pod=consumer: context deadline exceeded

```


• Root Cause: Both the serial and parallel event tests fail because the consumer pod in namespace ptp-event-framework-test does not emit logs within the deadline. This consumer pod is established by the event test setup and depends on the cloud-event-proxy sidecar publishing a SyncStateChange event; with ptp4l in FREERUN (Group 2), no valid sync-state transition is ever published, so the consumer pod log stream never produces the expected line and the context deadline fires. The parallel test independently hits the same consumer pod and likewise times out.

• Breaking PR/Commit: Cascade from Group 2; event framework code unchanged. Unknown if there is a separate event-consumer pod startup bug.

Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp


TL;DR: Hardware sync failures across RDU2 nodes and a deterministic PMC split-args code bug together account for 36 test failures spanning all 7 suites.



Root Cause Groups


#DescriptionCountSuites
1T-GM ts2phc stuck in FREERUN on cnfdf32 — DPLL shows LOCKED but ts2phc reports FREERUN; daemon gate blocks phc2sys, clockClass never reaches 6, cascading to event/metric/holdover failures11 / 36tgm
2BC slave port ens2f0np0 / hardware clock sync degradation — BC slave stuck in MASTER state; ptp4l clockClass stuck at 248 (FREERUN) on dualnicbc nodes; cascading to config, event-consumer, and interface-recovery tests~14 / 36dualnicbc (5–6), dualnicbcha (8–9)
3PMC split-args bug in getClockIDViaPMC — commits 3b93c9f408 / d20ffcbf0c pass "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET" as two separate argv elements; pmc rejects both with bad command; all ClockSync tests time out deterministically~5 / 36dualnicbc (3), dualnicbcha (2)
4Parallel event soak test timeout (OCPBUGS-60570 interaction) — PushInitialEvent retry loop (up to 30 × 10 s = 300 s) shares the same 6-minute soak timer; release-5.0 image fix (OCPBUGS-60570) slows initial event delivery, exhausting the budget before LOCKED is received; all 5 parallel suites hit this simultaneously pointing to a cluster-wide event delivery slowdown5 / 36bc (1), dualfollower (1), oc (1), dualnicbc (1), dualnicbcha (1)
5No T-BC topology on cluster — CreatePtpConfigurationsWithRetry finds 0 T-BC L2 solutions on cnfdf30–32; execute.BeforeAll calls Fail() instead of Skip(), failing the first spec and silently skipping the rest1 / 36tbc


Cross-Suite Patterns


• Hardware sync failure is the dominant cross-suite thread. Root causes 1 and 2 both point to the RDU2 test nodes (cnfdf30–32) failing to maintain a healthy PTP grandmaster-to-slave chain during this job window. tgm (ts2phc FREERUN on the GM node) and dualnicbc/dualnicbcha (clockClass/port-state failures on BC nodes) are facets of the same degraded physical sync fabric.

• The PMC split-args bug (root cause 3) is strictly test-code and suite-independent. It affects every suite that exercises the getClockIDViaPMC fallback path — currently triggered only in dualnicbc and dualnicbcha because their log format misses the primary log-parsing path. bc-serial escapes because it locates the clock ID via log parsing before reaching the broken fallback.

• The parallel soak timeout (root cause 4) is cross-suite by construction. All five parallel sub-suites (bc-parallel, dualfollower-parallel, dualnicbc-parallel, dualnicbcha-parallel, oc-parallel) run the same testSyncState test against the same cluster-event infrastructure. Their simultaneous failure at ≈363 seconds is a single shared event, not five independent regressions.

• Suite-specific failures: tbc's BeforeAll topology failure is isolated to that suite; tgm's ts2phc FREERUN affects only the GM node tests.


Actionable Recommendations


1. Fix the PMC split-args bug immediately (highest leverage, deterministic, trivially patched).

In test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go (around line 144), change:

```go

// current (broken):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"}

// fix:

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET PARENT_DATA_SET"}

```

This matches the existing pattern in ptptesthelper.go:588 (GetClockClassViaPMC) and will immediately unblock ~5 deterministically failing tests in dualnicbc and dualnicbcha.


2. Investigate and remediate the RDU2 hardware sync chain (cnfdf30–32).

Both the ts2phc FREERUN (tgm) and the BC slave MASTER-state / clockClass-248 failures (dualnicbc, dualnicbcha) trace to the physical PTP grandmaster-to-slave path being degraded during this run window. Check GNSS/GPS signal quality on the GM node, verify the T-GM NIC (ens7fx/WPC card) cable and SFP state, and confirm DPLL lock propagation from GM to BC nodes before re-running.


3. Decouple PushInitialEvent retries from the soak timer, and add a Skip path for missing topologies.

For root cause 4: run the PushInitialEvent retry loop before starting tcEndChan, or extend the parallel soak window to accommodate the OCPBUGS-60570 slow-start behavior.

For root cause 5 (tbc): replace the Fail("Could not create a ptp config…") call in execute.BeforeAll with a Skip(...) when no topology is found, preventing misleading failures when the cluster lacks T-BC hardware.



Overall Issue Class


infra_other + test_regression (mixed: ~21 failures are hardware/infra-driven; ~5 are a deterministic test code bug; 5 are a test/infra interaction flake; 1 is a topology mismatch)


Overall Severity


HIGH — 36 failures spanning all 7 suites; two root causes are entirely blocking for their affected suites (ts2phc FREERUN, BC slave MASTER state), and one is a trivially fixable deterministic code regression that has been silently breaking ClockSync tests across at least two suites.




Per-Suite Details



bc



Suite: bc (1 failures)


Suite TL;DR: The single bc failure is the event-based PTP Slave Clock Sync test timing out because the OS clock never reached LOCKED state (as reported via PTP events) within the test's monitoring window.


Root Cause Groups:


• Group 1: OS clock never reported LOCKED via PTP events within test duration (affects: [It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync)
• Evidence:
• From investigation-summary.txt: Source: parallel_suite_test.go:117, parallel_suite_test.go:90, ptp.go:393, run.go:84
• From telco5g-ptp-tests__test_results.json: "[It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync": {"time": 363.837272163, "result": "error"}
• From ptp.go (line 392–393): if !wasLocked { Fail("OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out") }
• From ptp.go (lines 355, 371–373): const maxPushInitialEventAttempts = 30 … for i = 0; i < maxPushInitialEventAttempts; i++ { err = event.PushInitialEvent(string(ptpEvent.OsClockSyncStateChange), 10*time.Second)
• From ci-operator-build-log.txt (line 40–42): + export PTP_UNDER_TEST_BRANCH=release-5.0 … + export IMG_VERSION=release-5.0
• From ci-operator-build-log.txt (line 37): + export TEST_BRANCH=main — test scripts run from main against release-5.0 production images
• Root Cause: In test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go, the testSyncState function subscribes to OsClockSyncStateChange events and waits up to the configured soak-test duration for the OS clock to report LOCKED. The test ran for 363 seconds (≈ ~60 s of PushInitialEvent retries + a ~5-minute soak window), matching the tcEndChan path at ptp.go:393. Commit 4aa5310 on main ("ci: fix timeout onPushInitialEvent") introduced the 30-retry loop specifically because OCPBUGS-60570 changed release-5.0 cloud-event-proxy to only serve CurrentState from real PTP socket data. Despite eventually getting an initial event, the OsClockSyncStateChange events never carried a LOCKED state before the soak period expired — indicating the OS clock did not lock during that window on the test cluster. This same pattern recurs in all five parallel suites (bc-parallel, dualfollower-parallel, dualnicbc-parallel, dualnicbcha-parallel, oc-parallel), pointing to a systemic sync or event-delivery problem rather than a BC-specific regression.
• Breaking PR/Commit: Upstream behavioral change tracked in OCPBUGS-60570 (backported to release-5.0 cloud-event-proxy images); test-side adaptation landed in main commit 4aa5310 ("ci: fix timeout onPushInitialEvent"). No single cherry-pick SHA identified as the trigger; the OCPBUGS-60570 image change is the underlying cause.
• Is it a flake? Possibly — the identical test failing simultaneously across all five parallel suites in the same run (bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc) suggests a systemic cluster-level sync failure for this specific run rather than a permanent regression. The test has a documented history of timing sensitivity (hence commit 4aa5310). A single retry of the periodic job is warranted before escalating.
• Suggested Fix: Verify whether the BC node's OS clock is actually achieving LOCKED state during test runs by inspecting phc2sys logs; if the clock is locking but events aren't delivered, investigate whether the release-5.0 cloud-event-proxy OsClockSyncStateChange publication path is broken. If this is reproducible, raise a bug against the release-5.0 cloud-event-proxy image referencing OCPBUGS-60570 and confirm the fix is correctly backported.

3PMC split-args bug in getClockIDViaPMC — commits 3b93c9f408 / d20ffcbf0c pass "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET" as two separate argv elements; pmc rejects both with bad command; all ClockSync tests time out deterministically~5 / 36dualnicbc (3), dualnicbcha (2)

Cross-Suite Patterns


• Hardware sync failure is the dominant cross-suite thread. Root causes 1 and 2 both point to the RDU2 test nodes (cnfdf30–32) failing to maintain a healthy PTP grandmaster-to-slave chain during this job window. tgm (ts2phc FREERUN on the GM node) and dualnicbc/dualnicbcha (clockClass/port-state failures on BC nodes) are facets of the same degraded physical sync fabric.

• The PMC split-args bug (root cause 3) is strictly test-code and suite-independent. It affects every suite that exercises the getClockIDViaPMC fallback path — currently triggered only in dualnicbc and dualnicbcha because their log format misses the primary log-parsing path. bc-serial escapes because it locates the clock ID via log parsing before reaching the broken fallback.

• The parallel soak timeout (root cause 4) is cross-suite by construction. All five parallel sub-suites (bc-parallel, dualfollower-parallel, dualnicbc-parallel, dualnicbcha-parallel, oc-parallel) run the same testSyncState test against the same cluster-event infrastructure. Their simultaneous failure at ≈363 seconds is a single shared event, not five independent regressions.

• Suite-specific failures: tbc's BeforeAll topology failure is isolated to that suite; tgm's ts2phc FREERUN affects only the GM node tests.


Actionable Recommendations


1. Fix the PMC split-args bug immediately (highest leverage, deterministic, trivially patched).

In test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go (around line 144), change:

```go

// current (broken):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"}

// fix:

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET PARENT_DATA_SET"}

```

This matches the existing pattern in ptptesthelper.go:588 (GetClockClassViaPMC) and will immediately unblock ~5 deterministically failing tests in dualnicbc and dualnicbcha.


2. Investigate and remediate the RDU2 hardware sync chain (cnfdf30–32).

Both the ts2phc FREERUN (tgm) and the BC slave MASTER-state / clockClass-248 failures (dualnicbc, dualnicbcha) trace to the physical PTP grandmaster-to-slave path being degraded during this run window. Check GNSS/GPS signal quality on the GM node, verify the T-GM NIC (ens7fx/WPC card) cable and SFP state, and confirm DPLL lock propagation from GM to BC nodes before re-running.


3. Decouple PushInitialEvent retries from the soak timer, and add a Skip path for missing topologies.

For root cause 4: run the PushInitialEvent retry loop before starting tcEndChan, or extend the parallel soak window to accommodate the OCPBUGS-60570 slow-start behavior.

For root cause 5 (tbc): replace the Fail("Could not create a ptp config…") call in execute.BeforeAll with a Skip(...) when no topology is found, preventing misleading failures when the cluster lacks T-BC hardware.

infra_other + test_regression (mixed: ~21 failures are hardware/infra-driven; ~5 are a deterministic test code bug; 5 are a test/infra interaction flake; 1 is a topology mismatch)


Overall Severity


HIGH — 36 failures spanning all 7 suites; two root causes are entirely blocking for their affected suites (ts2phc FREERUN, BC slave MASTER state), and one is a trivially fixable deterministic code regression that has been silently breaking ClockSync tests across at least two suites.

Suite: bc (1 failures)


Suite TL;DR: The single bc failure is the event-based PTP Slave Clock Sync test timing out because the OS clock never reached LOCKED state (as reported via PTP events) within the test's monitoring window.


Root Cause Groups:


• Group 1: OS clock never reported LOCKED via PTP events within test duration (affects: [It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync)
• Evidence:
• From investigation-summary.txt: Source: parallel_suite_test.go:117, parallel_suite_test.go:90, ptp.go:393, run.go:84
• From telco5g-ptp-tests__test_results.json: "[It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync": {"time": 363.837272163, "result": "error"}
• From ptp.go (line 392–393): if !wasLocked { Fail("OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out") }
• From ptp.go (lines 355, 371–373): const maxPushInitialEventAttempts = 30 … for i = 0; i < maxPushInitialEventAttempts; i++ { err = event.PushInitialEvent(string(ptpEvent.OsClockSyncStateChange), 10*time.Second)
• From ci-operator-build-log.txt (line 40–42): + export PTP_UNDER_TEST_BRANCH=release-5.0 … + export IMG_VERSION=release-5.0
• From ci-operator-build-log.txt (line 37): + export TEST_BRANCH=main — test scripts run from main against release-5.0 production images
• Root Cause: In test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go, the testSyncState function subscribes to OsClockSyncStateChange events and waits up to the configured soak-test duration for the OS clock to report LOCKED. The test ran for 363 seconds (≈ ~60 s of PushInitialEvent retries + a ~5-minute soak window), matching the tcEndChan path at ptp.go:393. Commit 4aa5310 on main ("ci: fix timeout onPushInitialEvent") introduced the 30-retry loop specifically because OCPBUGS-60570 changed release-5.0 cloud-event-proxy to only serve CurrentState from real PTP socket data. Despite eventually getting an initial event, the OsClockSyncStateChange events never carried a LOCKED state before the soak period expired — indicating the OS clock did not lock during that window on the test cluster. This same pattern recurs in all five parallel suites (bc-parallel, dualfollower-parallel, dualnicbc-parallel, dualnicbcha-parallel, oc-parallel), pointing to a systemic sync or event-delivery problem rather than a BC-specific regression.
• Breaking PR/Commit: Upstream behavioral change tracked in OCPBUGS-60570 (backported to release-5.0 cloud-event-proxy images); test-side adaptation landed in main commit 4aa5310 ("ci: fix timeout onPushInitialEvent"). No single cherry-pick SHA identified as the trigger; the OCPBUGS-60570 image change is the underlying cause.
• Is it a flake? Possibly — the identical test failing simultaneously across all five parallel suites in the same run (bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc) suggests a systemic cluster-level sync failure for this specific run rather than a permanent regression. The test has a documented history of timing sensitivity (hence commit 4aa5310). A single retry of the periodic job is warranted before escalating.
• Suggested Fix: Verify whether the BC node's OS clock is actually achieving LOCKED state during test runs by inspecting phc2sys logs; if the clock is locking but events aren't delivered, investigate whether the release-5.0 cloud-event-proxy OsClockSyncStateChange publication path is broken. If this is reproducible, raise a bug against the release-5.0 cloud-event-proxy image referencing OCPBUGS-60570 and confirm the fix is correctly backported.

dualnicbc



Suite: dualnicbc (11 failures)


Suite TL;DR: A split-args bug in the newly introduced getClockIDViaPMC helper causes PMC commands to be rejected by the pmc binary, timing out all ClockSync tests; cascading config disruption and an event-consumer timeout account for the remaining failures.



Root Cause Groups:


• Group 1: PMC split-args bug in getClockIDViaPMC (affects: Slave can sync to master, Downstream slave can sync to BC master, Can provide a profile with higher priority)

• Evidence:

```

parentPortIdentity.clockIdentity not found in pmc output for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config: bad command: GET

bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET

grandmasterIdentity not found in pmc output for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config: bad command: GET

bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET

Timed out after 203.731s. / 203.074s. / 201.562s.

```


• Root Cause: getClockIDViaPMC in test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go (introduced in commit d20ffcbf0c, merged via 855c9e1493 2026-07-07) passes the pmc batch command as two separate slice elements — "GET" and "PARENT_DATA_SET" — rather than the single combined string "GET PARENT_DATA_SET":

```go

// BUGGY (ptphelper.go:144):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"}

// CORRECT (ptptesthelper.go:588, same repo):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET PARENT_DATA_SET"}

```

The linuxptp pmc binary processes each remaining argv element as a complete batch command. Receiving "GET" alone produces bad command: GET; "PARENT_DATA_SET" alone produces bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET. The getClockIDViaPMC fallback (reached when log-regex parsing misses the dualnicbc log format) therefore always fails, and the Eventually wrapper (3-minute timeout) exhausts before returning, failing these tests. bc-serial passes the equivalent tests because it finds the clock ID via log parsing and never reaches the broken pmc fallback.


• Breaking PR/Commit: d20ffcbf0c / merged 855c9e1493 — _"CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash"_ — test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go — [https://github.com/openshift/ptp-operator/commit/855c9e1493](https://github.com/openshift/ptp-operator/commit/855c9e1493)

• Is it a flake? No — the split-args bug produces bad command on every invocation, deterministically.

• Suggested Fix: Merge the two separate args into one in ptphelper.go: change "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET" to "GET PARENT_DATA_SET" as a single slice element, consistent with how GetClockClassViaPMC in ptptesthelper.go:588 already invokes pmc.


• Group 2: ptp4l clock class stuck at FREERUN (248) (affects: Verify clockClass when locking PTP source on dual NIC boundary clock, Should recover clockClass via event API after cloud-event-proxy crash, BC clock class recovers to Locked after upstream link outage)

• Evidence:

```

Timed out after 300.000s.

Expected PMC clock class 6 for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config

Expected : 248

to equal : 6

Timed out after 300.000s.

Expected ptp4l clock class to eventually be 6 for GM

Expected : false

to be true

```


• Root Cause: By the time these tests run (>670 s into the suite), test 3 ("Can provide a profile with higher priority") has timed out at 261 s while the temporary high-priority PtpConfig "temp" was still active. Although DeferCleanup(RestorePtp4lConf) fires, the ensuing ptp4l restart on the dualnicbc node means the second ptp4l instance (ptp4l.1) must re-acquire lock. The clockClass tests' 5-minute Eventually windows overlap with this re-sync period. Additionally, EnableGMCapableInPlace (used in test 4 at ptp.go:1256) explicitly injects clockClass 248 into the PtpConfig to create test conditions; if RestorePtp4lConf does not take effect fast enough before subsequent polling, all three clockClass assertions see 248. The correct GetClockClassViaPMC call format ("GET PARENT_DATA_SET" as a single arg at ptptesthelper.go:588) rules out the same pmc bug.

• Breaking PR/Commit: Same 855c9e1493 (test-ordering/cleanup-timing consequence of the Group 1 regression); no independent code regression confirmed for this group.

• Is it a flake? Partially — the cascade is deterministic given Group 1's timeouts, but the exact re-sync window makes this timing-sensitive.

• Suggested Fix: Fix Group 1 first; additionally add a post-DeferCleanup wait for ptp4l re-lock before handing off to the next test, and ensure EnableGMCapableInPlace is always accompanied by a synchronous restore check.


• Group 3: Interface role and process-state cascade (affects: The slave node network interface is taken down and up, Should restart phc2sys with no socket errors after SIGTERM, PTP metric is present verifies on slave)

• Evidence:

```

Timed out after 300.001s.

ens2f0np0 should recover to SLAVE

incorrect role for ens2f0np0, role expected=1(SLAVE), role observed=2(MASTER)


Timed out after 180.001s.

Expected phc2sys process status to be 1 for GM

Expected : 0

to equal : 1


Timed out after 300.000s.

Time metrics are not detected

```


• Root Cause: With ptp4l.1 in FREERUN (clock class 248, no upstream lock — see Group 2), the port that should be SLAVE (ens2f0np0) remains in MASTER role because ptp4l acts as a grandmaster candidate. phc2sys does not start when ptp4l is unlocked (process status=0). PTP time-sync metrics (openshift_ptp_*) are not emitted without a locked clock state. All three symptoms are downstream of the same unlocked ptp4l.1 state, compounded by the config disruption from Group 1/2.

• Breaking PR/Commit: Same cascade from 855c9e1493. No independent breaking commit identified.

• Is it a flake? No — deterministic cascade.

• Suggested Fix: Resolving Group 1 and ensuring clean state restore between tests (Group 2) should clear these failures.


• Group 4: Event consumer pod log deadline (affects: Should receive events after linuxptp-daemon pod restart, [dualnicbc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync)

• Evidence:

```

getCurrentState did not return SyncStateChange

error reading logs in ns=ptp-event-framework-test pod=consumer: context deadline exceeded


could not push initial event, err=error reading logs in ns=ptp-event-framework-test pod=consumer: context deadline exceeded

```


• Root Cause: Both the serial and parallel event tests fail because the consumer pod in namespace ptp-event-framework-test does not emit logs within the deadline. This consumer pod is established by the event test setup and depends on the cloud-event-proxy sidecar publishing a SyncStateChange event; with ptp4l in FREERUN (Group 2), no valid sync-state transition is ever published, so the consumer pod log stream never produces the expected line and the context deadline fires. The parallel test independently hits the same consumer pod and likewise times out.

• Breaking PR/Commit: Cascade from Group 2; event framework code unchanged. Unknown if there is a separate event-consumer pod startup bug.

The test ran for ~363 seconds without ever receiving a LOCKED event. The simultaneous failure of the same event-based test across all 5 parallel suites (bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc), plus serial PTP-sync failures in dualnicbc/dualnicbcha/tgm/tbc suites in the same run, points to the PTP grandmaster-to-slave synchronization chain being degraded or disconnected on the RDU2 test hardware during this job window rather than any code regression.
• Breaking PR/Commit: Unknown — no code change identified; this is a hardware/infrastructure timing failure. Test code on main already includes commit 4aa5310 (ci: fix timeout onPushInitialEvent) which extended PushInitialEvent retries to 30×10s for exactly this class of slow-start scenario. The release-5.0 images are built from release-5.0 branch. No new cherry-pick or release-5.0 code change identified as a trigger.
• Is it a flake? yes — simultaneous failure across 5 independent parallel suites on the same hardware node pool at the same wall-clock time is the hallmark of a transient infra condition (PTP GM link loss, NIC reset, or environmental timing glitch), not a reproducible code defect. The dualfollower serial suite's configuration-verification tests all passed in the same run.
• Suggested Fix: Re-run the job to confirm this is transient. If it recurs, check whether the PTP grandmaster at cnfdf30/cnfdf31/cnfdf32 (RDU2 telco5g lab) was in holdover or FREERUN during the test window by examining the must-gather artifacts and pod-logs collected at post-step; longer-term, the test could be made more resilient by retrying the entire soak test when zero LOCKED events are observed within the first few minutes.

Suite Issue Class: test_flake

Suite Severity: MEDIUM


dualnicbc



Suite: dualnicbc (11 failures)


Suite TL;DR: A split-args bug in the newly introduced getClockIDViaPMC helper causes PMC commands to be rejected by the pmc binary, timing out all ClockSync tests; cascading config disruption and an event-consumer timeout account for the remaining failures.



Root Cause Groups:


• Group 1: PMC split-args bug in getClockIDViaPMC (affects: Slave can sync to master, Downstream slave can sync to BC master, Can provide a profile with higher priority)

• Evidence:

```

parentPortIdentity.clockIdentity not found in pmc output for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config: bad command: GET

bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET

grandmasterIdentity not found in pmc output for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config: bad command: GET

bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET

Timed out after 203.731s. / 203.074s. / 201.562s.

```


• Root Cause: getClockIDViaPMC in test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go (introduced in commit d20ffcbf0c, merged via 855c9e1493 2026-07-07) passes the pmc batch command as two separate slice elements — "GET" and "PARENT_DATA_SET" — rather than the single combined string "GET PARENT_DATA_SET":

```go

// BUGGY (ptphelper.go:144):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET"}

// CORRECT (ptptesthelper.go:588, same repo):

[]string{"pmc", "-b", "0", "-u", "-f", configFile, "GET PARENT_DATA_SET"}

```

The linuxptp pmc binary processes each remaining argv element as a complete batch command. Receiving "GET" alone produces bad command: GET; "PARENT_DATA_SET" alone produces bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET. The getClockIDViaPMC fallback (reached when log-regex parsing misses the dualnicbc log format) therefore always fails, and the Eventually wrapper (3-minute timeout) exhausts before returning, failing these tests. bc-serial passes the equivalent tests because it finds the clock ID via log parsing and never reaches the broken pmc fallback.


• Breaking PR/Commit: d20ffcbf0c / merged 855c9e1493 — _"CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash"_ — test/pkg/ptphelper/ptphelper.go — [https://github.com/openshift/ptp-operator/commit/855c9e1493](https://github.com/openshift/ptp-operator/commit/855c9e1493)

• Is it a flake? No — the split-args bug produces bad command on every invocation, deterministically.

• Suggested Fix: Merge the two separate args into one in ptphelper.go: change "GET", "PARENT_DATA_SET" to "GET PARENT_DATA_SET" as a single slice element, consistent with how GetClockClassViaPMC in ptptesthelper.go:588 already invokes pmc.


• Group 2: ptp4l clock class stuck at FREERUN (248) (affects: Verify clockClass when locking PTP source on dual NIC boundary clock, Should recover clockClass via event API after cloud-event-proxy crash, BC clock class recovers to Locked after upstream link outage)

• Evidence:

```

Timed out after 300.000s.

Expected PMC clock class 6 for /var/run/ptp4l.1.config

Expected : 248

to equal : 6

Timed out after 300.000s.

Expected ptp4l clock class to eventually be 6 for GM

Expected : false

to be true

```


• Root Cause: By the time these tests run (>670 s into the suite), test 3 ("Can provide a profile with higher priority") has timed out at 261 s while the temporary high-priority PtpConfig "temp" was still active. Although DeferCleanup(RestorePtp4lConf) fires, the ensuing ptp4l restart on the dualnicbc node means the second ptp4l instance (ptp4l.1) must re-acquire lock. The clockClass tests' 5-minute Eventually windows overlap with this re-sync period. Additionally, EnableGMCapableInPlace (used in test 4 at ptp.go:1256) explicitly injects clockClass 248 into the PtpConfig to create test conditions; if RestorePtp4lConf does not take effect fast enough before subsequent polling, all three clockClass assertions see 248. The correct GetClockClassViaPMC call format ("GET PARENT_DATA_SET" as a single arg at ptptesthelper.go:588) rules out the same pmc bug.

• Breaking PR/Commit: Same 855c9e1493 (test-ordering/cleanup-timing consequence of the Group 1 regression); no independent code regression confirmed for this group.

• Is it a flake? Partially — the cascade is deterministic given Group 1's timeouts, but the exact re-sync window makes this timing-sensitive.

• Suggested Fix: Fix Group 1 first; additionally add a post-DeferCleanup wait for ptp4l re-lock before handing off to the next test, and ensure EnableGMCapableInPlace is always accompanied by a synchronous restore check.


• Group 3: Interface role and process-state cascade (affects: The slave node network interface is taken down and up, Should restart phc2sys with no socket errors after SIGTERM, PTP metric is present verifies on slave)

• Evidence:

```

Timed out after 300.001s.

ens2f0np0 should recover to SLAVE

incorrect role for ens2f0np0, role expected=1(SLAVE), role observed=2(MASTER)


Timed out after 180.001s.

Expected phc2sys process status to be 1 for GM

Expected : 0

to equal : 1


Timed out after 300.000s.

Time metrics are not detected

```


• Root Cause: With ptp4l.1 in FREERUN (clock class 248, no upstream lock — see Group 2), the port that should be SLAVE (ens2f0np0) remains in MASTER role because ptp4l acts as a grandmaster candidate. phc2sys does not start when ptp4l is unlocked (process status=0). PTP time-sync metrics (openshift_ptp_*) are not emitted without a locked clock state. All three symptoms are downstream of the same unlocked ptp4l.1 state, compounded by the config disruption from Group 1/2.

• Breaking PR/Commit: Same cascade from 855c9e1493. No independent breaking commit identified.

• Is it a flake? No — deterministic cascade.

• Suggested Fix: Resolving Group 1 and ensuring clean state restore between tests (Group 2) should clear these failures.


• Group 4: Event consumer pod log deadline (affects: Should receive events after linuxptp-daemon pod restart, [dualnicbc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync)

• Evidence:

```

getCurrentState did not return SyncStateChange

error reading logs in ns=ptp-event-framework-test pod=consumer: context deadline exceeded


could not push initial event, err=error reading logs in ns=ptp-event-framework-test pod=consumer: context deadline exceeded

```


• Root Cause: Both the serial and parallel event tests fail because the consumer pod in namespace ptp-event-framework-test does not emit logs within the deadline. This consumer pod is established by the event test setup and depends on the cloud-event-proxy sidecar publishing a SyncStateChange event; with ptp4l in FREERUN (Group 2), no valid sync-state transition is ever published, so the consumer pod log stream never produces the expected line and the context deadline fires. The parallel test independently hits the same consumer pod and likewise times out.

• Breaking PR/Commit: Cascade from Group 2; event framework code unchanged. Unknown if there is a separate event-consumer pod startup bug.
